description: Fractional CMO services cost $3K-$15K/mo for senior marketing leadership. Compare pricing, scope, and how to get matched in 48 hours.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to hire a fractional CMO?

acceptedAnswer.text: Through a general search or referral network, expect two to six weeks of sourcing, interviewing, and negotiating. Through a vetted talent platform like MarketerHire, you can be matched with a qualified fractional CMO in 48 hours and start a paid trial the same week.

mainEntity.name: Can a fractional CMO manage my existing marketing team?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Team leadership is a core part of the fractional CMO role. They set strategic direction, run weekly standups, and hold team members accountable to KPIs. Many fractional CMOs also manage external vendors and agencies on your behalf, consolidating all marketing team oversight under one leader.

mainEntity.name: What industries do fractional CMOs work in?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fractional CMOs work across B2B SaaS, e-commerce and DTC, professional services, healthcare, financial services, and consumer technology. The model is most common at companies with $2M to $50M in revenue. Industry-specific experience matters, so prioritize CMOs who have worked in your vertical or a closely related one.

mainEntity.name: How is a fractional CMO different from a marketing consultant?

acceptedAnswer.text: A marketing consultant advises and delivers recommendations, often as a one-time project. A fractional CMO owns your marketing function: they set strategy, manage the team, control the budget, and carry accountability for pipeline and revenue outcomes. Consultants hand you a plan. Fractional CMOs execute the plan and own the results.

mainEntity.name: Is a fractional CMO worth it for a startup?

acceptedAnswer.text: For startups between seed and Series B with $1M to $20M in revenue, a fractional CMO is often the most efficient path to building a marketing function. You get senior strategic leadership without committing $300K+ to a full-time hire. The key is finding someone with startup experience.
